Human–Robot Interaction Study: Human–Robot Collaborative Assembly



Principal Investigator: Prof. Mohsen Moghaddam 

Researchers: Seok Joon Kim, Dante Santaniello

Institution: Georgia Institute of Technology 

Laboratory: SAIL Lab (ISyE) - George Tower 1224

IRB Protocol Number:  IRB2025-320



1. Purpose of the Study 

Welcome, and thank you for your interest in this study.

You are invited to participate in a research study investigating how humans interact and collaborate with robots during assembly tasks.

The purpose of this study is to better understand how people communicate their intentions, request assistance, and work together with a robot during a co-assembly process. The findings from this study may help inform the design of more intuitive, effective, and user-friendly human–robot collaboration systems.



2. Structure of the Study

If you agree to participate, you will complete 4 studies. It is estimated to take 1.5 hours. 



3. Data That May Be Collected During the study

The researchers may collect information about your interaction with the robotic system, including:



-Task completion time and task performance

-Assembly errors or corrections

-Robot movements and system logs

-Requests for parts, tools, or assistance

-Verbal descriptions, commands, or other spoken interactions

-Hand, head, and pointing movements through Meta Quest3

-Interaction timestamps

-Video and/or audio recordings

-Questionnaire responses



The collected data will be used for research and related academic purposes only and will NOT be shared to public. 



4. Potential Risks or Discomforts 

The risks associated with this research are expected to be minimal.

Possible risks or discomforts include:


-Mild physical or mental fatigue from performing the assembly task.
-Temporary frustration or confusion while interacting with the robot.
-Mild discomfort from wearing an augmented or virtual reality headset.
-Motion sickness, eye strain, dizziness, or headache when using a headset.
-Accidental contact with the robot or objects in the workspace.



The robotic system will operate under researcher supervision, and appropriate safety measures will be used. You will receive instructions regarding safe interaction with the robot before beginning the experiment. You should not intentionally enter restricted areas of the robot workspace unless instructed by the researcher. You may stop the experiment immediately if you feel uncomfortable or unsafe.



5. Compensation

You will receive 15 USD for participating in this study.



6. Confidentiality 

Reasonable measures will be taken to protect your privacy and the confidentiality of your research data. Your research data will be associated with a participant identification number rather than your name whenever possible. Data may be stored on password-protected computers, secure institutional storage systems, or encrypted research servers accessible only to authorized members of the research team.



Results from this study may be presented in: Scientific publications such as Conference papers, Academic presentations Theses or dissertations, Research demonstrations.



7. Voluntary Participation

Your participation in this study is completely voluntary. You may: Decline to participate. Refuse to perform any activity that makes you uncomfortable. Ask questions at any time. Stop participating at any time without penalty. 



8. Stopping the Experiment 

You should immediately inform the researcher if you experience:

-Physical discomfort

-Dizziness or nausea

-Significant eye strain Anxiety or distress

-Concern about the robot's behavior



The researcher may also stop the experiment if continuing the study could create a safety concern.



9. Questions About the Research

If you have questions about this research study, please contact:



Dr. Mohsen Moghaddam: Principal Investigator mohsem.moghaddam@gatech.edu

Seok Joon Kim: Main Researcher seokjoonkim@gatech.edu



For questions about your rights as a research participant or concerns about the conduct of the study, please contact:

Georgia Institute of Technology Institutional Review Board (IRB) (https://oria.gatech.edu/irb)
